followup_explanation:
This is a straightforward historical synthesis/summarization task — explaining a topic in a single constrained paragraph based on provided sources. That maps most closely to extraction/retrieval and summarization work.

Looking at the documentation:

- On **Summarization**, the two models are effectively tied (Willet 79.9 vs. Whimbrel 80.3 — well within the 2.0-point variance band).
- On **Extraction & Retrieval**, which matters here because the task asks to draw specific evidence from given sources, Whimbrel scores meaningfully higher (81.6 vs. 78.5, a gap above the variance threshold).

The content is benign academic history, so the models' differing preference profiles around harm-adjacent material don't come into play, and neither has a capability edge tied to those preferences anyway. Given the retrieval-from-sources component, Whimbrel's stronger Extraction & Retrieval profile made it the better fit, with everything else essentially equal.
